screening.reason: Reports a graph convolutional network diagnostic classification of ASD vs healthy controls using resting-state fMRI connectivity from ABIDE (Inclusion 2, 3)

evidence_spans.text:
The Autism Brain Imaging Data Ex-
change (ABIDE)1 [39] initiative aggregates resting-state
functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) and phe-
notypic data of 1112 subjects from various international
brain imaging laboratories. We select a set of 871 subjects,
consisting of 403 ASD patients and 468 healthy controls
(HCs).
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort was 871 of 1112 ABIDE subjects (403 ASD, 468 HC).

evidence_spans.text:
For preprocessing of
the ABIDE dataset, we use the Configurable Pipeline for the
Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC) [41], which includes skull
stripping, slice timing correction, motion correction, global
mean intensity normalization, nuisance signal regression, band-
pass filtering (0.01-0.1Hz), and registration of fMRI images to a
standard anatomical space. Then, the mean timeseries for a set
of cortical and subcortical regions of interest (ROIs) extracted
from the Har
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE data preprocessed with C-PAC and parcellated with the Harvard-Oxford atlas.

evidence_spans.text:
For the edge weights of the population graph
on the ABIDE datset, we incorporate the subject’s gender, age
and acquisition site as as phenotypic measures.
evidence_spans.claim: Site, age and gender are used as phenotypic edge-weight features in the population graph used for node classification.

evidence_spans.text: We use a stratified 10-fold cross-validation strategy.

evidence_spans.claim: Baseline GCN achieved 64.63% accuracy / 72.23% AUC on ABIDE.
The proposed AN-GCN achieved 96.91% accuracy and 96.86% AUC on ABIDE, far exceeding all baselines (best baseline DS-MML: 87.62% accuracy, 92.00% AUC).

evidence_spans.text:
the results show that our model outperforms all the base-
line methods on the ABIDE dataset, achieving relative improve-
ments of 50.33%, 34.10%, 50.33%, 12.25% and 50.33% over
GCN in terms of accuracy, AUC, F1-score, recall and precision,
respectively.
evidence_spans.claim: AN-GCN improved relative accuracy by 50.33% over the baseline GCN on ABIDE.

evidence_spans.text:
Hence, we take the upper triangular
part and vectorize it to obtain a feature vector whose dimension
is then further reduced using recursive feature elimination via a
ridge classifier.
evidence_spans.claim: Connectivity feature vectors are dimensionality-reduced via recursive feature elimination with a ridge classifier before the 10-fold CV procedure is described, with no statement that this is confined to training folds.

assessments.support: N by diagnosis (403 ASD/468 HC of 871 selected from 1112) is reported, though the exact selection/exclusion rule for the 871 is not detailed beyond "we select a set of 871 subjects".
C-PAC pipeline and Harvard-Oxford atlas are described in detail, with Fisher z-transformed Pearson correlation connectivity features.
ASD vs HC labels used without stating the diagnostic instrument/source.

Recursive feature elimination via a ridge classifier is described prior to the cross-validation section with no statement that it is confined to training folds; the population graph is built transductively using phenotypic data (including site) from all subjects before node classification; site is used as a graph-edge similarity feature rather than being held out or corrected for, and no leave-site-out evaluation is reported. The reported accuracy (96.91%) is far above both the baselines in this paper (best baseline 87.62%) and most published ABIDE benchmarks, consistent with a leakage-driven inflation.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort size and pipeline/atlas are well reported, but feature reduction (recursive feature elimination) appears to precede the stratified 10-fold cross-validation with no stated leakage control, the transductive population graph is built using all subjects' phenotypic data (including site) before fold assignment, and no leave-site-out check is reported; the resulting accuracy (96.91%) is implausibly high relative to the paper's own baselines and the published ABIDE literature, consistent with a leakage-driven result.

charting.title: Classification of Developmental and Brain Disorders via Graph Convolutional Aggregation
charting.disorder_diagnosis: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) vs healthy control (HC)
charting.feature_types: functional connectivity; phenotypic (gender, age, acquisition site used as graph edge weights)
charting.specific_features: Fisher z-transformed Pearson correlation connectivity matrices over Harvard-Oxford atlas ROIs; recursive-feature-elimination-reduced upper-triangular connectivity vector; population graph edges weighted by gender, age and acquisition site
charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC (Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes); Harvard-Oxford atlas
charting.model_category: Graph convolutional network (population-graph node classification) with attention/skip-connection aggregation
charting.specific_algorithms: AN-GCN (proposed), compared against Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting, GCN, InceptionGCN, EV-GCN, LGL, HI-GCN, MMGL, DeepGCN, DS-MML
charting.validation_methodology: Stratified 10-fold cross-validation; hyperparameters set via grid search with cross-validation on the training set
charting.performance_metrics: Accuracy, AUC, F1-score, Recall, Precision, Cohen's kappa, Matthews Correlation Coefficient
charting.key_performance_results: AN-GCN: 96.91% accuracy, 96.86% AUC, 97.16% F1, 96.91% recall, 97.00% precision on ABIDE, versus the strongest baseline DS-MML (87.62% accuracy, 92.00% AUC) and baseline GCN (64.63% accuracy, 72.23% AUC); a relative improvement of 50.33% in accuracy over GCN
charting.summary_key_findings: A population-graph GCN with skip connections and identity mapping (AN-GCN) classified ASD vs HC on 871 ABIDE subjects (403 ASD/468 HC) with 96.91% accuracy and 96.86% AUC, substantially exceeding all compared baselines including a strong recent method (DS-MML, 87.62% accuracy); feature reduction (recursive feature elimination) is described prior to the cross-validation step and site/age/gender are embedded directly as population-graph edge weights, raising a leakage/inflation concern given this result is far above both the paper's own baselines and typical published ABIDE benchmarks.
charting.reviewer_notes: Reported 96.91% accuracy is markedly higher than the paper's own strongest baseline (87.62%) and most published ABIDE classification results, consistent with the leakage risk noted (feature elimination preceding CV; transductive population graph using site/age/gender from all subjects).

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs HC); ABIDE (consistent with ABIDE I), 871 of 1112 subjects (403 ASD, 468 HC)
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI parcellated with the Harvard-Oxford atlas; Fisher z-transformed Pearson connectivity, dimensionality-reduced via recursive feature elimination; a transductive population graph (nodes = imaging features, edges weighted by gender/age/acquisition site) classified with a proposed attention/skip-connection GCN (AN-GCN), evaluated with stratified 10-fold cross-validation against several GCN-based baselines.
narrative_row.outcomes: AN-GCN achieved 96.91% accuracy and 96.86% AUC on ABIDE, far exceeding the strongest compared baseline (DS-MML, 87.62% accuracy, 92.00% AUC) and the basic GCN baseline (64.63% accuracy).
narrative_row.key_limitations: No diagnosis-source statement; feature elimination appears to precede the CV split; site/age/gender used directly as population-graph edge weights rather than controlled for, with no leave-site-out evaluation; the very high accuracy is substantially above the paper's own baselines and typical ABIDE benchmarks, suggesting possible leakage/inflation.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Illustrates a predictive, transductive population-graph GCN approach on ABIDE with a pipeline/atlas clearly reported but validation design raising leakage concerns given an unusually high accuracy.
